item.title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
item.description: arXiv:2610.30251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and $S^z$ conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe$_2$ and MoTe$_2$. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale, Trithep Devakul, Nicolas Regnault, Julian May-Mann

item.title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
item.description: arXiv:2610.30322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Pratap Kumar Pal, Moojune Song, Jinho Lim, Juliang Li, Serhii Kruhlov, Ralu Divan, Ulrich Welp, Clarence Chang, Kab-Jin Kim, Valentine Novosad, Axel Hoffmann, Yi Li

item.title: Nonlinear and Chaotic Dynamics of Two Dipolar-Coupled Anisotropic Spins under Periodic Excitation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we characterize how dipolar coupling, transverse driving amplitudes, and uniaxial anisotropy govern the long-time dynamics. The results reveal a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with alternating intervals of enhanced and suppressed instability. Analysis of symmetric and antisymmetric coordinates distinguishes the collective and relative spin responses, while Fourier spectra and three-dimensional trajectories provide complementary frequency-domain and geometrical characterizations. Simultaneous positivity of the two largest Lyapunov exponents identifies parameter regions consistent with hyperchaotic dynamics. Finally, analytical linearization and ferromagnetic-resonance calculations reveal the distinct coupling dependence of the collectivemode frequencies and clarify the limitations of the linearized description beyond the stability thresholds of the collinear reference state. These findings establish a unified framework for understanding the interplay of dipolar coupling, anisotropy, and periodic excitation in the non-linear dynamics of a minimal interacting-spin system.
item.dc:creator: Manish Anand

item.title: Spin polarization in a chiral ladder: elastic and inelastic environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.30419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the transport window and environmental reinjection determine the spin polarization transmitted through a minimal two-leg chiral ladder. The model contains time-reversal-invariant helical spin--orbit coupling, spin-independent interchain hopping, and nonmagnetic contacts with two orbital modes per lead. Sublattice symmetry makes the coherent spin-transmission kernel exactly odd in energy. A window centered on the symmetry point therefore gives zero integrated spin current, whereas a displaced window selects an uncanceled spectral interval. The resulting polarization reverses between enantiomers and vanishes in the decoupled-chain, zero-spin--orbit, and equivalent-strand limits of this model. We compare uniform absorption, energy-resolved elastic probes, and thermalized voltage probes at the same finite bias, including reinjection whenever probes are present. Charge conservation alone does not prohibit enhancement of the integrated spin signal: the elastic-probe response can increase at finite bias even where its linear-response counterpart decreases. Thermalized probes can also lift the centered-window zero that elastic probes preserve. Absorption and reinjection also change the transmitted charge, so enhancement of spin current and enhancement of normalized polarization must be distinguished. Static onsite disorder produces sample-dependent fluctuations; its signed ensemble mean is reported with uncertainty and is not forced to vanish in a displaced window. These results identify the energy interval and reservoir prescription that must be controlled when interpreting dephasing trends in minimal models relevant to chirality-induced spin selectivity.
item.dc:creator: D. T. Verrilli H., Jorge Cardenas-Gamboa, Mayra Peralta, Claudia Felser, Jos\'e H. Garcia, Solmar Varela, Nelson Bol\'ivar

item.title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
item.description: arXiv:2610.30453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm^3 N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = L{\sigma}/({\omega}{\epsilon}0{\epsilon}h), here, {\sigma} conductivity, {\omega} - cyclic frequency, {\epsilon}h,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano Zamengo, Meguya Ryu, Haoran Mu, Hsin-Hui Huang, Nguyen Hoai An Le, Tomas Katkus, Darius Gailevi\v{c}ius, Junko Morikawa, Saulius Juodkazis

item.title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
item.description: arXiv:2610.30502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\propto\tau_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhang

item.title: Finite-width altermagnetic quantum rings: angular-channel hybridization and Aharonov--Bohm physics
item.description: arXiv:2610.30536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a finite-width two-dimensional quantum ring with a quadratic $d$-wave altermagnetic term, Tan--Inkson confinement, a perpendicular magnetic field, and independently tunable Aharonov--Bohm (AB) flux. The altermagnetic interaction mixes $m$ and $m\pm2$ angular channels while preserving their parity. Circular symmetry renders the crystal orientation spectrally irrelevant and makes the two spin blocks exactly isospectral. The resulting same-parity anticrossings are resolved at low filling, and multichannel mixing is found near the Fermi level of highly occupied rings. Independent converged calculations for $N_e=1400$ and $1800$ establish the reconstructed Fermi edge and magnetic response in a finite field window and the persistent current over a full AB flux period. The analytic conventional reference separates radial-subband depopulation (dHvA-type cycles) from finer finite-ring shell oscillations; we do not assign a global Fourier spectrum to unverified altermagnetic field scans. The few-electron thermal response is obtained from an exact fixed-particle-number canonical partition function, avoiding finite-system errors of a fixed-mean-number approximation. The circular model supports an equilibrium charge current but no persistent spin current.
item.dc:creator: Edilberto O. Silva

item.title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.30733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.
item.dc:creator: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang

item.title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
item.description: arXiv:2610.30743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Xiao, Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu

item.title: Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector
item.description: arXiv:2610.30905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a monolithic telecom C-band single-photon platform based on low-density InAs/InP quantum dots grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector, with simulated upward light-extraction efficiency exceeding 10% within the 40 nm spectral band. Enhanced light extraction is crucial for wide-field photoluminescence imaging, enabling approximately 3 nm statistical centroid-localization precision of QD emitters due to improved signal-to-noise ratio. The identified charged exciton emitting at 1549.5 nm exhibits single-photon emission purity up to 94.7%, validated by a raw peak-area integration under pulsed quasi-resonant excitation. Under these conditions, photons emitted sequentially from the unprocessed planar structure reveal a raw two-photon interference visibility of 51% of the photon wave packet within the 2 ns time window and 41% over a 4 ns integration window, all without Purcell enhancement typical for cavity-embedded emitters. Combining broadband extraction, high photon coherence, and emitter preselection on a native III-V wafer, this architecture paves the way for marker-based deterministic fabrication of high-quality monolithic nanophotonic devices.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Mrowi\'nski, Jan \'Smigiel, Miko{\l}aj Badura, Beata \'Sciana, Wojciech Kijaszek, Emilia Zi\k{e}ba-Ost\'oj, Pawe{\l} Holewa, Marcin Syperek

item.title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
item.description: arXiv:2610.31508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.
item.dc:creator: Arpan De, William Livernois, Simon Vecchioni, Yoel P. Ohayon, M. P. Anantram

item.title: Einstein's theory of Brownian motion: The non-Fickian normal diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.30194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Einstein's theory of diffusion defines what is considered {\it normal diffusion}. Historically, Einstein considered homogeneous diffusion characterised by a diffusion constant in his original calculations, resulting in what is known as {\it Fickian} diffusion, which thermally relaxes concentration inhomogeneities. However, in the same derivation of Einstein, the seed of generalisation of the theory to {\it non-Fickian} diffusion in the presence of space-dependent diffusivity is hidden. This indicates that non-Fickian diffusion, which can drive concentration inhomogeneities, can also be normal diffusion. The present article discusses the origin of the {\it normal} non-Fickian diffusion in Einstein's theory of diffusion.
item.dc:creator: A. Bhattacharyay

item.title: Piezo-Kerr effect in altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets
item.description: arXiv:2610.30929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them. Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system. Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state. Enumerating all 122 MPGs, we identify 16 groups in which the unstrained Kerr response is forbidden while a linear strain-induced contribution is allowed. These groups are realized by altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets with symmetry-enforced vanishing net magnetization. The active strain channels and the associated first-order sign reversals follow directly from symmetry. First-principles calculations for bulk MnTe$_{2}$ and CoF$_{2}$, and Cr$_{2}$Se$_{2}$O and Cr$_{2}$Te$_{2}$O monolayers confirm these predictions. In these materials, the Kerr rotation vanishes without strain, whereas 0.5-3% strain produces rotations ranging from tens to hundreds of millidegrees, and reversing the matched strain channel reverses the Kerr sign. These results establish a general route to large and switchable Kerr responses emerging from symmetry-forbidden states in compensated magnets.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Liu, Qiu-Shi Huang, Xinfeng Chen, Yilin Han, Run-Wu Zhang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao

item.title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
item.description: arXiv:2610.31067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Haiting Zhang, Lei Xiao, Cui-Xian Guo, Quan Lin, Peng Xue

item.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
item.description: arXiv:2610.31242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase \(\gamma_n\). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is \(\gamma_n\)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.
item.dc:creator: Longyan Gong, Jing Zhang, Yongtao Li

item.title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Weed

item.title: Quantum geometry and quantum capacitance in the orbital magneto-electric effect
item.description: arXiv:2505.02911v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The orbital magneto-electric effect (OME), the generation of a steady-state orbital angular momentum (OAM) density by an electric field, is a central component of orbitronics. Nevertheless its microscopic interpretation is complicated by the existence of two qualitatively different contributions: the intra-band Edelstein term stemming from the combined effect of the equilibrium OAM and Fermi surface shift, and the inter-band contribution, stemming from Zitterbewegung induced by the electric field. Here we develop a pedagogical density-matrix formulation of the OME within the framework of the modern theory of Bloch-electron OAM, in which the two contributions naturally emerge from distinct parts of the density matrix, and their distinct quantum geometric structures are clearly seen. In the inter-band contribution, in addition to the local- and itinerant-circulation terms, we show that a band-diagonal displacement, or charge dipole, is present, which is linear in the electric field and governed by the normalized quantum metric. For a tilted massive Dirac cone the Zitterbewegung OME and the Fermi-surface orbital response occur for orthogonal electric-field orientations, providing a route to separate them experimentally. The itinerant-circulation contribution is identical to the dipolar one, so in a two-band model the dipole accounts for exactly half of the inter-band response, both in the doped regime and in the insulating gap. Our recent insights identify quantum-metric engineering as a route for enhancing orbital magneto-electric responses and clarify the relation between modern orbital magnetization, polarization, and orbital torque phenomenology.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J.H.Cullen, D.P.Arovas, R.Raimondi, and D.Culcer, (2026). Advances in Physics, 1-26
item.dc:creator: James H. Cullen, Daniel P. Arovas, Roberto Raimondi, Dimitrie Culcer

item.title: The ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene: Dynamical skyrmion lattices and their excitations
item.description: arXiv:2511.07402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. This dynamical skyrmion lattice naturally leads to experimentally measurable consequences. In particular, we identify new collective excitations corresponding to chiral shape deformations of the skyrmions, and propose a new positively charged quasiparticle, the skyrmion vacancy. These results establish a qualitatively new form of moir\'e Chern physics in rhombohedral graphene: an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice whose skyrmions are dynamical low-energy degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Tixuan Tan, Patrick J. Ledwith, Trithep Devakul

item.title: Electrostatic edge effects versus edge doping in graphene nanoribbons: a scanning gate microscopy and modelling study
item.description: arXiv:2602.12944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The charge neutrality point (CNP) of graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) patterned by oxygen plasma etching moves towards zero as the ribbon narrows and, on 300 nm SiO2, changes sign below a crossover width of ~ 50 nm: an observation previously attributed to n-type edges surrounding a p-type bulk. We test this edge-doping hypothesis in three ways. First, finite element modelling of complete GNR transistors with uniform doping shows that fringing of the gate field at the edges reproduces the trend of the measured CNP with width down to ~ 50nm without any edge doping, while producing a bias-dependent inversion of the carrier type at the edges that mimics n-type edges in scanned-probe measurements. Second, fitting the CNP of ribbons on 90 nm and 300 nm SiO2 with the gate capacitance of a finite strip, which fixes the electrostatic contribution with no adjustable parameter other than the bulk doping, shows that fringing accounts for most of the width dependence and isolates the remainder as an edge charge. This is acceptor-like (0.24 e/nm per edge) in the present ribbons, which therefore have no n-type edges, and donor-like but small in devices on 300 nm SiO2; no single edge-charge, field-coupled or contact-doping mechanism describes both. Third, scanning gate microscopy finds no edge contrast of the sign expected for n-type edges. The width dependence of the CNP is therefore predominantly electrostatic, and n-type edges are not an intrinsic consequence of oxygen-plasma etching. A design map shows that fringing dominates the width dependence whenever the gate dielectric is thicker than 30-50 nm, whereas in scaled high-K transistors, edge charge dominates and would shift the threshold voltage of a 10 nm ribbon by ~ 0.1-0.15 V. Fitting the CNP versus width with the strip capacitance provides a simple test for edge doping in any gated two-dimensional nanostructure
item.dc:creator: Colm Durkan, Xiao Liu, Ed Saunders

item.title: Dipole-exchange spin waves and mode hybridization in magnetic nanoparticles
item.description: arXiv:2603.24187v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate spin-wave modes in confined ferromagnetic resonators with spherical and cylindrical geometries across the exchange-dominated, dipole-exchange, and dipolar interaction regimes. Starting from the linearized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, we show that the projection of the total angular momentum and mirror parity are conserved quantities in the problem of axially symmetric resonators. These symmetries provide a natural classification of spin-wave modes and explain the degeneracy of exchange modes, as well as its lifting by dipolar interactions. Numerical analysis shows that the nonlocal dipolar interaction removes the exchange degeneracy and hybridizes modes, leading to avoided crossings between modes that belong to the same symmetry sector. To describe this behavior, we develop a coupled-mode theory formulated directly in terms of dynamical magnetization, which reduces the dipole-exchange problem to a finite system of interacting modes. The resulting framework provides a unified description of spin-wave spectra in confined magnetic particles from the exchange limit to the dipolar regime.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Shuklin, Khristina Albitskaya, Sergei Solovyov, Alexander Chernov, Mihail Petrov

item.title: Parity-driven RKKY decoupling and anomalous $1/R$ Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in odd-parity magnets
item.description: arXiv:2607.10757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unconventional odd-parity magnets, characterized by an odd-parity momentum-dependent spin splitting, offer a fundamentally distinct paradigm for non-collinear spintronics. Here, we theoretically investigate the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida indirect exchange in two-dimensional odd-parity magnets subjected to Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Using an analytical real-space Green's function formalism, we uncover a parity-driven spatial decoupling in the magnetic response. Because of the odd-parity exchange field, the out-of-plane Ising interaction is structurally insulated from the macroscopic magnetic modulation, oscillating isotropically at the shifted Fermi wavevector. Conversely, the in-plane Heisenberg components exhibit pronounced, directionally tunable spatial beating. Beyond collinear exchange, the hybridized bands generate a highly tunable, three-component Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction alongside symmetric off-diagonal anisotropies. We reveal that the out-of-plane chiral twisting is driven by the massive, nonrelativistic momentum shift, while the in-plane chiral components are relativistic. Furthermore, the competition between the nodal geometry and the Rashba gap drives an anomalous, dimension-reducing crossover, in which the in-plane chiral components follow a 1D-like $1/R$ spatial decay along the nodal lines over an extended intermediate-distance window before ultimately recovering the conventional 2D $1/R^2$ asymptote. We demonstrate that these findings hold universally across the odd-parity class by explicitly generalizing our framework to $f$-wave magnets. Finally, numerical tight-binding calculations verify the striking robustness of this parity-driven decoupling against both scalar and random magnetic exchange disorder. These findings establish odd-parity magnets as promising platforms for engineering robust, directionally tunable non-collinear spin textures.
item.dc:creator: Morteza Salehi, Tohid Farajollahpour

item.title: Electronic properties and topological aspects of graphene nanohelicoids
item.description: arXiv:2607.13294v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce graphene nanohelicoids, geometric analogs of graphene nanoribbons, in which the honeycomb lattice is embedded on a helicoidal surface. Starting from the three-dimensional helical structure, we construct effective one-dimensional lattice models with band structures characterized by a momentum-shifted particle-hole relation $E_v(k)=-E_c(k+\pi)$ that reflects an antichiral symmetry arising from the nonsymmorphic symmetry. A systematic investigation of graphene nanohelicoids using the tight-binding approximation reveals a number of trends upon varying width and edge orientation, for instance, alternating transitions between semiconducting and metallic regimes. As the structure width varies, the band gap periodically closes and reopens, accompanied by an alternating Zak phase that switches between trivial and nontrivial. Using an analytic tight-binding model with a continuous deformation of the graphene nanohelicoids, we explain the origin of width- and termination-dependent band inversion and alternating Zak phase, and derive the relationship between the termination-resolved index and the sublattice symmetry operator in one-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoqian Liu, Arsen Herasymchuk, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Oleg V. Yazyev

item.title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2608.02513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. We trace this back to suppressed phonon-mediated scattering from bright to dark excitons. Furthermore, we predict a periodic modulation of the transient exciton diffusion in the presence of a compressive strain resulting from strain-driven emission of M phonons. The gained microscopic insights illustrate how strain can be used to engineer transient photoluminescence and exciton diffusion in technologically promising 2D semiconductors.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic

item.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moir\'e Hubbard bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.22307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Moir\'e semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to about 50mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.
item.dc:creator: Yiyu Xia, Yichi Zhang, Zhongdong Han, Hongyuan Li, Brandon Bauer, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wenjin Zhao, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak

item.title: Many-Body effects beyond excitons in second-harmonic generation of monolayer MoS$_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2602.22463v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a quantitative study of many-body effects including the three-particle level on second-harmonic generation in monolayer MoS$_2$. Our approach combines many-body perturbation theory with time-dependent current-density-functional theory within an \textit{ab initio} framework in the optical limit. The inclusion of two-particle excitonic effects \textit{via} a dynamical long-range linear exchange-correlation kernel reproduces the qualitative features of the second-harmonic response, but differs from the experimentally reported magnitude by nearly a factor of two. By incorporating three-particle trionic correlations through a static long-range quadratic exchange-correlation kernel, we achieve significantly improved quantitative agreement with experiment for the three main bound excitonic resonances. These findings suggest that many-body interactions beyond the two-body excitonic level can play an important role in accurately describing second-order optical responses in two-dimensional semiconductors.
item.dc:creator: Peio Garcia-Goiricelaya, Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz

item.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation with Quantum Feedback
item.description: arXiv:2602.22651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its role within the TUR framework has remained unclear, particularly in quantum systems where control is inherently information-driven. In this Letter, we consider open quantum systems weakly coupled to a thermal environment, in which quantum jumps are continuously monitored, and Markovian feedback is applied. Using quantum mutual information to quantify the information contribution induced by feedback, we derive a finite-time TUR for arbitrary time-integrated currents in terms of entropy production and mutual information. Our results uncover how feedback control suppresses fluctuations together with thermodynamic cost and establish a fundamental precision bound imposed by information-based control. As an application, we analyze a quantum clock model and demonstrate that the clock precision can be enhanced by feedback control in the presence of a single thermal reservoir.
item.dc:creator: Ryotaro Honma, Tan Van Vu

item.title: A Photonic Tautochrone: Spatiotemporal Beam Focusing for Enhanced Nonlinear Response
item.description: arXiv:2603.03691v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose to implement an optical analogue of the tautochrone property of the cycloid to allow the focusing of ultrashort pulses inside photonic systems. This allows to enhance nonlinear effects, resulting in orders of magnitude increase of nonlinearity-induced phase shifts, while employing low irradiances. Building upon the optical-mechanical analogy, we show how to produce optical limiters for temporal light pulses, and how to implement temporal bistability and even multistability with large numbers of states. Finally, we move this concept to the quantum realm and predict a tautochrone quantum blockade regime with a stronger antibunching.
item.dc:creator: W. Verstraelen, S. Zanotti, N. W. E. Seet, J. Zhao, D. Sanvitto, J. Zu\~niga-Perez, K. Dini, Y. G. Rubo, T. C. H. Liew

item.title: Chiral Transport in Metric-Affine Geometries
item.description: arXiv:2606.04841v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anomalous transport in equilibrium fermionic fluids chirally coupled to background Weyl-type nonmetricity is studied. A formal descent analysis is carried out in which the dependence of the anomaly polynomial on the nonmetricity tensor is encoded in a Weyl invariant four-form. The constitutive relation of the axial-vector current is evaluated from the equilibrium partition function obtained using transgression techniques, showing the existence of nonmetricity-mediated chiral separation effects driven by the fluid's vorticity and the Weyl magnetic field. A second nonminimal coupling of fermionic matter to metric-affine geometries proposed in the literature is also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. Vazquez-Mozo

item.title: Selective strain tuning of nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics in BiFeO$_\text3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.29472v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum materials are characterized by intertwined orders, and a fundamental goal in condensed matter physics is to achieve their selective control in such a way that one order parameter can be tuned while leaving others largely unaffected. Although significant progress has been made in thermal equilibrium, realizing such control out of equilibrium remains highly challenging. Here we employed in-situ tensile strain to selectively manipulate the photoinduced lattice dynamics associated with ferroelectric and magnetic orders in multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. By applying MeV ultrafast electron diffraction to freestanding BiFeO$_3$ membranes under tunable strain, we showed that tensile strain markedly suppresses the ultrafast photoinduced reduction of the ferroelectric displacement. By contrast, the photoinduced dynamics of the antiferrodistortive rotation of the oxygen octahedra, which modulates the magnetic order, remains insensitive to strain. Not only do these findings reveal distinct microscopic pathways underlying nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics, they also establish tunable strain as an effective route for engineering ultrafast phase control in correlated materials.
item.dc:creator: Chenhang Xu, Patrick Liu, Bo Zhang, Minyong Han, Henry G. Bell, Cameron J. R. Duncan, Yusong Liu, Patrick L. Kramer, Randy Lemons, Jake D. Koralek, Alexander H. Reid, Dong Qian, Harold Y. Hwang, Alfred Zong

item.title: Transition-Metal Chalcogenide Nanowires: A First-Principles Study of Stability, Electronic Structure, and Mechanical Response
item.description: arXiv:2610.15214v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Subnanometer transition-metal chalcogenide nanowires provide a one-dimensional platform in which electronic functionality and mechanical response can be tuned through chemical composition. Here, density functional theory calculations are combined with machine-learning force-field (MLFF) molecular dynamics to investigate MoS, MoSe, MoTe, WS, WSe, and WTe nanowires. The optimized structures are dynamically stable within the harmonic approximation, and their electronic character evolves systematically across the chalcogen series: MoS, MoSe, WS, and WSe are metallic, whereas MoTe and WTe are semiconducting, with HSE06 band gaps of 0.52 and 0.20 eV, respectively. The effective axial stiffness decreases from sulfides to selenides and tellurides, consistent with the increase in metal--chalcogen bond length; using a circular effective cross section, the corresponding Young moduli range from 392 to 718 GPa. All six nanowires have negative formation energies relative to the selected elemental reference phases. MLFF trajectories extending to 2.5 ns at 300 K preserve the one-dimensional morphology and local atomic order, providing evidence of finite-temperature dynamical stability on the simulated time scale. The corresponding MLFF molecular-dynamics energy traces are shown in. We further examine the response of the nanowires to axial strain and curvature, including strain-induced band-gap modulation in the tellurides. These results establish composition and mechanical deformation as complementary routes for tuning the electronic and mechanical properties of ultrathin transition-metal chalcogenide nanowires and support their further investigation as components of flexible nanoelectronic systems.
item.dc:creator: Danilo de Ara\'ujo Moura, Flavio Bento de Oliveira, Andreia Luisa da Rosa
